Train a custom BirdNET classifier from R

Source: R/birdnet_train.R
pam_birdnet_train.Rd

Runs BirdNET-Analyzer's own birdnet-train command inside pamflow's training environment, so the trained model is the same kind of file the Analyzer GUI produces. The training runs in a separate process: an error or crash cannot take down your R session.

Usage

pam_birdnet_train(
  data_dir,
  output,
  params = list(),
  test_data = NULL,
  load_params = NULL,
  cache_mode = NULL,
  cache_file = NULL,
  envdir = pam_birdnet_env_dir("training"),
  live = FALSE,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  log_dir = NULL
)

Arguments

data_dir

Training folder with one sub-folder per class. Use pam_birdnet_train_prepare() first.

output

Output path prefix, e.g. "E:/models/MyModel". The Analyzer writes <output>.tflite, <output>_Labels.txt, <output>_Params.csv and <output>_sample_counts.csv. pamflow adds <output>_run.yml (what was run) and <output>_train.log (everything the trainer printed) and uses <output>_cache.npz only if you set cache_mode.

params

Named list of training parameters. Names: epochs, val_split, learning_rate, batch_size, threads, crop_mode, overlap, fmin, fmax, audio_speed, hidden_units, dropout, focal_loss, focal_loss_gamma, focal_loss_alpha, label_smoothing, mixup, upsampling_ratio, upsampling_mode, model_save_mode, model_format ("tflite", "raven" or "both"), autotune, autotune_trials, autotune_executions_per_trial. Yes/no options are on/off switches: TRUE turns them on, FALSE leaves them off. Anything you do not set is left to the installed Analyzer, so a plain run uses the same defaults as that version's own command line. The values it actually used are written to <output>_Params.csv.

test_data

Optional separate test folder; if NULL the Analyzer holds out val_split of the training data.

load_params

Optional path to an earlier run's parameters file, passed as --load_params. Only Analyzer versions that provide that option accept it; otherwise pamflow stops with a clear message.

cache_mode

NULL (default), "save" or "load": passed as --cache_mode. Left off by default so a plain run behaves exactly like the Analyzer. With "load" the features are read from cache_file instead of the audio (the training folder may then be NULL).

cache_file

Cache file for cache_mode; defaults to <output>_cache.npz. A relative path is taken relative to the folder of output, not the working directory.

envdir

Training environment folder (from pam_birdnet_setup("training")).

live

If TRUE, also show the trainer's output on the console while it runs. The log file is written either way.

overwrite

If FALSE (default), refuse to overwrite an existing model.

log_dir

Optional folder for a log file (birdnet_train.log).

Value

Invisibly, a list: status ("ok" or "failed"), output, files (named logical: which expected files exist), elapsed (difftime), log, run_record, args, and metrics (from pam_birdnet_train_metrics(), NULL if the log could not be read) and evaluation (with a separate test_data folder: a list with overall, classes and path read from <output>_evaluation.csv, one row per class with precision, recall, F1, AUPRC and AUROC; otherwise NULL) and, when a cache was used, cache (what the trainer reported: see pam_train_cache_notes()).

Details

This is a standalone tool: it is not a stage of the workflow and no workflow function calls it. Use the trained model by pointing the birdnet: section of the config at it.

This is a standalone tool, not a pipeline stage: it needs no config file and nothing in the workflow calls it. Assumptions: BirdNET-Analyzer is installed in the training environment and provides the birdnet-train command. Hyperparameter autotuning needs the Analyzer's train extra (pam_birdnet_setup("training", packages = "birdnet-analyzer[train]", recreate = TRUE)). Before running, pamflow checks that every option it passes appears in the installed birdnet-train --help and stops with a clear message if one does not.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
prep <- pam_birdnet_train_prepare("E:/training_clips")
res <- pam_birdnet_train("E:/training_clips", "E:/models/MyModel",
                         params = list(epochs = 100, hidden_units = 512))
# reproduce an earlier run from its parameters file
pam_birdnet_train("E:/training_clips", "E:/models/Rerun",
                  load_params = "E:/models/BirdNet_v2_custom_Params.csv")
} # }
